idiom_name: lazy stored property + throwing validateForPublish() gate at the call site
implementation_notes: Swift makes deferral a property modifier and pushes the failure to the caller: a lazy stored property is calculated on first access rather than at initialisation, and a throwing method invoked from the action site is the gate, because try moves the error to the caller - which is the deferral the pattern asks for. Result or Optionals carry the outcome where throwing is too heavy, and value types make it cheap to validate a snapshot, while property observers (willSet/didSet) are the eager opposite and should not be used for invariant checks on objects meant to be assembled over time. A separate validator type is still warranted when the same rule set serves several types.
pitfalls: A lazy var on a struct copies its pending state: a copy taken before first access can run the validation independently, so the same draft validates twice and the two copies keep separate results.
The check runs on any access to the lazy property, including a debug description or a diffing framework, so keep it private and expose only the throwing gate.
Stored properties cannot throw - only functions can - so the gate must be a method or a failable initialiser, and a forgotten call leaves the raw value readable without ever being checked.
